statement: Negotiated contracts and subcontracts of $35 million or less are exempt from all CAS requirements; the value is tested at award, using the ceiling for indefinite-delivery contracts and each order under a multiple-award contract.
quote: Negotiated contracts and subcontracts not in excess of $35 million.
note: Was $2.5 million before 2026-10-01; the same rule ended the $7.5 million trigger contract (91 FR 56056, S-0028). 9903.201-1(c) sets how the value is tested.

statement: Full CAS coverage applies to a business unit that receives a single CAS-covered award of $100 million or more, or $100 million or more in net CAS-covered awards in its preceding cost accounting period.
quote: Receive a single CAS-covered contract award of $100 million or more
note: Was $50 million before 2026-10-01 (S-0028); 9903.201-2(b)(4) lets units move to modified coverage.

statement: A business unit selected for a CAS-covered contract or subcontract of $100 million or more must submit a Disclosure Statement before award.
quote: Any business unit that is selected to receive a CAS-covered contract or subcontract of $100 million or more shall submit a Disclosure Statement before award.

statement: When a DoD contracting officer's final determination on material weaknesses in a contractor business system includes a notice to withhold, the contracting officer withholds 5 percent of amounts due from progress and performance-based payments.
quote: the Contracting Officer will withhold 5 percent of amounts due from progress payments and performance-based payments
note: The same paragraph directs the contractor to withhold 5 percent from interim cost vouchers. Total withholds may not exceed 5 percent for one system or 10 percent for several (e)(2).

statement: The penalty for unallowable costs in final indirect cost rate proposals applies to contracts over $1 million, except the excluded fixed-price types.
quote: This section applies to all contracts in excess of $1 million, except fixed-price contracts without cost incentives or any firm-fixed-price contracts for the purchase of commercial products or commercial services.
note: RFO 42.508-1(b) (S-0019) renumbers it with the same wording; DoD uses it under Class Deviation 2026-O0050.

statement: The customary progress payment rate for DoD contracts with large business concerns is 80 percent.
quote: are 80 percent for large business concerns and 90 percent for small business concerns.
note: Same rate as codified DFARS 232.501-1(a) (S-0009). The codified FAR rate is 80 percent (FAR 32.501-1(a)).

statement: The customary progress payment rate for DoD contracts with small business concerns is 90 percent.
quote: are 80 percent for large business concerns and 90 percent for small business concerns.
note: The codified FAR small business rate is 85 percent (FAR 32.501-1(a)); DoD uses 90.

statement: On a fully funded cost-reimbursement contract with the Limitation of Cost clause, the contractor must notify the contracting officer when costs expected in the next 60 days, added to costs incurred, will exceed 75 percent of the estimated cost.
quote: will exceed 75 percent of the estimated cost specified in the Schedule
note: The codified prescription lets the 60 days vary from 30 to 90 and the 75 percent from 75 to 85; read the clause in the contract.

statement: Under the codified FAR, certified cost or pricing data are required above $2.5 million for prime contracts awarded on or after July 1, 2018, unless an exception applies.
quote: The threshold for obtaining certified cost or pricing data is $950,000 for prime contracts awarded before July 1, 2018, and $2.5 million for prime contracts awarded on or after July 1, 2018.
note: Not the DoD rule after June 30, 2026: see CL-EST-0002. RFO 15.403-3(a) says meets or exceeds; the codified text says expected to exceed.

statement: For DoD prime contracts awarded after June 30, 2026, certified cost or pricing data are required when the contract is expected to exceed $10 million, unless an exception at FAR 15.403-2 or DFARS 215.403-71 applies.
quote: obtain certified cost or pricing data when a prime contract is expected to exceed $10 million and is awarded after June 30, 2026
note: Replaces FAR 15.403-3(a) for DoD. Subcontracts under primes entered on or before June 30, 2026 keep $2.5 million, and so does a modification under such a subcontract (pp. 23-24). Effective date is the memo's signature date; it says effective immediately.

statement: The simplified acquisition threshold is $350,000, with higher values for the listed contingency and defense purposes.
quote: Simplified acquisition threshold means $350,000, except for—
note: Raised from $250,000 by the inflation rule effective 2025-10-01 (S-0031). RFO 2.101 (S-0015) has the same value.

statement: The micro-purchase threshold is $15,000, with the listed exceptions.
quote: Micro-purchase threshold means $15,000, except it means—
note: Raised from $10,000 by the inflation rule effective 2025-10-01 (S-0031). RFO 2.101 (S-0015) has the same value.

statement: Except for the exempt contracts, for DoD cost or incentive contracts and subcontracts of $50 million or more, the earned value management system must comply with the EIA-748 guidelines.
quote: For cost or incentive contracts and subcontracts valued at $50 million or more, the clause at 252.234-7999, Earned Value Management System, requires
note: Codified DFARS 234.201(1)(i) (S-0010) still says $20,000,000. Effective date is the memo's signature date; it says effective immediately. The (j) exemptions (contracts primarily for software, or awarded to nontraditional defense contractors) apply; the HCA may waive them (pp. 6-7). Rev 1 supersedes 2026-O0011 of 2025-12-18, not stored, so whether these values started then is unconfirmed.

statement: Except for the exempt contracts, for DoD cost or incentive contracts and subcontracts of $100 million or more, the contractor must have an earned value management system the cognizant agency has determined compliant.
quote: For cost or incentive contracts and subcontracts valued at $100 million or more, the clause at 252.234-7999, Earned Value Management System, requires the contractor to have an earned value management system
note: Codified DFARS 234.201(1)(ii) (S-0010) still says $50,000,000. The (j) exemptions (contracts primarily for software, or awarded to nontraditional defense contractors) apply; the HCA may waive them (pp. 6-7). Rev 1 supersedes 2026-O0011 of 2025-12-18, not stored, so whether these values started then is unconfirmed.

statement: Under the Allowable Cost and Payment clause, a contractor must submit an adequate final indirect cost rate proposal within 6 months after the end of each fiscal year; the clause allows reasonable extensions for exceptional circumstances only.
quote: within the 6-month period following the expiration of each of its fiscal years
note: RFO 52.216-7 (S-0020) has the same wording; DoD uses it under Class Deviation 2026-O0038.
